title: Rogers-Ramanujan and Schur Partition Identities
description: Formalizes the Rogers-Ramanujan and Schur partition identities in Lean 4. Defines partition sets via gap conditions and modular arithmetic, states the identities as axioms (verified computationally), and proves structural properties including that gap ≥ 2 partitions are necessarily distinct.

meta.author: Rogers (1894), Ramanujan (1913), Schur (1926), formalized in Lean 4

originalContributions: Gap ≥ 2 implies distinct: proved that any partition with minimum gap 2 between consecutive parts has all distinct parts, via Pairwise strict inequality on the sorted parts list
RR2 ⊆ RR1: proved the containment of second Rogers-Ramanujan gap partitions in the first
Identified and removed false theorem: rr1Mod5Partitions ⊆ distincts is false (counterexample: 1+1+1 = 3)

overview.historicalContext: The Rogers-Ramanujan identities are among the most remarkable results in partition theory. First discovered by Rogers in 1894, independently rediscovered by Ramanujan around 1913, and later connected to statistical mechanics (Baxter's hard hexagon model, 1981) and vertex operator algebras (Lepowsky-Wilson, 1984).
overview.problemStatement: Can we formalize the Rogers-Ramanujan and Schur partition identities and prove structural relationships between the partition sets?
overview.proofStrategy: We define partition sets using decidable predicates on Nat.Partition, state the main identities as axioms (they require q-series machinery not yet in Mathlib), and prove structural theorems about containment relationships between partition classes. The key proof shows that gap ≥ 2 implies distinctness by establishing a Pairwise (· > ·) relation on the sorted parts list.
keyInsights: Gap ≥ 2 between consecutive sorted parts implies all parts are distinct, proved via List.Pairwise transitivity
The mod-5 partition sets (parts ≡ 1,4 mod 5) do NOT form a subset of distinct partitions — partition 1+1+1 = 3 is a counterexample
The correct hierarchy is: All ⊃ Distinct ⊃ Gap ≥ 2 (RR1) ⊃ Gap ≥ 2 + min ≥ 2 (RR2)

sections.title: Partition Gap Conditions
sections.summary: Defines hasMinGap for lists and partitions, checking minimum difference between consecutive elements in decreasing sorted order.

sections.title: Rogers-Ramanujan and Schur Partition Sets
sections.summary: Defines the six partition sets: RR1/RR2 gap and mod-5 partitions, and Schur gap and mod-3 partitions.

sections.title: Structural Properties
sections.summary: Proves gap ≥ 2 implies distinct parts, RR2 ⊆ RR1, and the correct containment hierarchy.

conclusion.summary: The formalization defines 6 partition sets, states 3 deep identities as axioms (Rogers-Ramanujan I & II, Schur), and proves 3 structural theorems with 0 sorries. The key contribution is proving that gap ≥ 2 implies distinctness and identifying a false theorem in the original formulation.
conclusion.implications: The Rogers-Ramanujan identities connect partition theory to q-series, statistical mechanics, and representation theory. Full proof would require formalizing q-series or bijective constructions.
openQuestions: Can the Rogers-Ramanujan identities be proved via q-series in Lean using PowerSeries from Mathlib?
Can a bijective proof (e.g., Garsia-Milne involution) be formalized?
Can the connection to the hard hexagon model be made formal?
